cards.text: God's been teaching Israel how His people are to live, and now He gives Moses, Israel's leader, another message to pass on. No small talk. He opens with who's talking: "I am the LORD your God."

Then God names two lands whose practices Israel must NOT follow: the one they used to live in, and the one He's bringing them into. That's like a new boss saying, "Don't do it like your last job, and DON'T do it like the guy down the hall."

cards.question: God says don't follow the practices of the land Israel used to live in, or of the land He's bringing them into. Which two lands are they?
So how DOES Israel live? Not Egypt's way and not Canaan's way. God tells them to work out a way of their own somewhere in between.
God tells Israel to keep His statutes and His judgments. What does He say about the man who does these things?

answers.text: He will be rich by them

cards.text: Then comes a long list. God says none of them are to approach any close relative to have sexual relations, and He walks through the family one by one, from mother and sister to aunt and daughter-in-law, then adds a neighbor's wife. Over and over He gives the reason, like it would dishonor a father or shame the family.
Then God brings up Molech, a god the Ammonites worshiped (1 Kings 11:7). And He draws a hard line.

cards.question: What does God say Israel must never give to be sacrificed to Molech?
God says giving a child to Molech would ___ the name of their God.

cards.text: God's still giving Moses His message for Israel. A man must not lie with a man as with a woman, which God calls an abomination, and no one is to lie with an animal, which He calls a perversion.
Now God steps back and looks at the whole list. He says, "Do not defile yourselves by any of these practices," and then He tells them why.

cards.question: God says the ___ He is driving out before Israel have defiled themselves by all these things.
God says even the land has become defiled, and He is punishing it for its sin. What will the land do to its inhabitants?

cards.text: Friend, I've been pushed off a counter and into a junk drawer, but I have NEVER had the ground itself kick me out. Then God says it plainly: Israel is to keep His statutes and ordinances and not commit any of these abominations.

cards.question: God says only the native-born Israelites must keep these rules, not the foreigner who lives among them.

cards.text: Then God reminds them: the men who were in the land before them committed all these abominations, and the land became defiled.

cards.question: Since God is bringing Israel into the land, He says it will never vomit them out, no matter what they do there.
What does God say must happen to anyone who commits any of these abominations?

answers.text: He must be cut off from his people
He must offer a lamb at the altar
He must stay outside the camp a week

cards.question: God wraps up by telling Israel to keep His charge and stay away from the customs practiced before them. Then He closes with the same words He opened with. What are they?

answers.text: I am the LORD your God
Hear O Israel the LORD is one
The LORD bless you and keep you

cards.text: That's where this message lands, friend. But God's not done teaching His people what it looks like to be His, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: The joke's comparison doesn't match the core action. Leviticus 18:3 is about two lands: the one Israel left and the one God is bringing them into. 'The guy down the hall' is a neighbor, not the place you're headed, so the second half of the comparison doesn't line up with Canaan.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The setup card (card 7) only says God 'draws a hard line,' so nothing lets the baker reason toward children over cattle or firstfruits. The pick comes down to luck, and this walkthrough already leans on several discovery questions (stop 1 card 5, stop 2 cards 4 and 9).

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'praise' and 'honor' aren't believable. A baker who knows God forbids the act can rule them out at once, so 'profane' stands out as the only possible pick.

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin was 'pushed off a counter and into a junk drawer.' His backstory says he was picked up, carried across the kitchen and slid into the drawer. The joke adds a new event to his story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: 'I am the LORD your God' is a repeated line. It appears in 18:2 and 18:4 before 18:30, and card 1 quotes it word for word. Asking about it at its last appearance breaks the repeated-line rule, and the answer was already given on card 1.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The summary card for the long stretch (18:6-20) has 3 sentences. The bite-sized rules say every story card after the opening card is 1 to 2 sentences, but the good genealogy example in the long-stretch section has 4 sentences.
findings.question: Does the 1-to-2-sentence limit apply to a summary story card for a long stretch, or can that card run longer, as the Genesis 5 example does?
